name: Man of the Woods
body:
Man of the Woods CR 7

XP 3,200
NG Huge outsider (native)
Init +1; Senses low-light vision; Perception +18

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 7, flat-footed 21 (–1 Dex, +14 natural, –2 size)
hp 79 (10d8+40)
Fort +13, Ref +3, Will +9
Immune outsider traits; DR 5/metal

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft. (40 ft. in forest)
Melee 2 slams +16 (2d6+7)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 15 ft.
Spells Known (CL 6th)

3rd (2/day)—plant growth, quench
2nd (3/day)—barkskin, summon nature’s ally II, tree shape
1st (3/day)—obscuring mist, speak with animals, goodberry, entangle
0 (4/day)—light, mending, stabilize, resistance

STATISTICS

Str 25; Dex 11; Con 21; Int 12; Wis 16; Cha 13
Base Atk +9; CMB +20; CMD 29
Feats Alertness, Improved Sunder, Iron Will, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (slam)
Skills Diplomacy +13, Intimidate +13, Knowledge (nature) +21, Perception +18, Sense Motive +15, Stealth +14
Languages Sylvan, Treant

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Spell-Like Abilities (Sp)

A man of the woods can cast pass with trace and wood shape at will as an 6th level druid.

ECOLOGY

Environment any forest
Organization solitary, pair, or trinity (3)
Treasure standard

Ever elusive, the man of the woods spends his days tending to his forest home. While these fey creatures share much of their life work and purpose with treants, they are different in mindset and approach to humanoid races. A man of the wood is far more likely to actively impede and impair trappers, hunters, and loggers in their demesne, but will typically resort to combat only when their forest is directly endangered.

A man of the woods is 8 feet tall, and weighs 400 pounds. They are covered with bark and lichen, and are often mistaken for a tree or treant. Their hair is coarse and matted, and they often adorn themselves with plant-based paint or mud to further enhance their natural appearance.
